cards.name: View
cards.summary: A saved named view from the View Manager docker (IVGView): it stores a page, a zoom level and a view origin so a script or user can jump back to that exact framing later. It is a bookmark of the camera, not the live window (that is Window.ActiveView).
use_for: bookmark the framing of each panel of a multi-page brochure so a review macro can step through them
jump back to a fixed close-up of a logo detail before taking a screen grab
build a client walkthrough of a layout from a list of saved framings
avoid: changing what the open window shows without saving anything: use Window.ActiveView (ToFitPage, Zoom, SetViewArea)
setting export bounds: a view only changes the screen; export a page or a ShapeRange instead
cards.how: Members live on IVGView. Saved views belong to a document: ActiveDocument.Views.Item(index or name). Create one with ActiveDocument.CreateView(Name, OriginX, OriginY, [Zoom], [Page]), or capture the current framing with ActiveDocument.Views.AddActiveView(Name). Activate applies the view to the active window; Delete removes it from the View Manager.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: read or rename the view as listed in the View Manager

key_members.name: OriginX
key_members.use: horizontal position the view jumps to (document units)

key_members.name: OriginY
key_members.use: vertical position the view jumps to (document units)

key_members.name: UseZoom
key_members.use: when True, Activate applies the stored Zoom

key_members.name: Page
key_members.use: the page the view belongs to (IVGPage)

key_members.name: UsePage
key_members.use: when True, Activate switches to the stored Page

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: apply the saved framing to the active window

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Views collection that holds it

gotchas: UseZoom / UsePage are switches: with one of them False, Activate keeps the window's current zoom (or page), so a view can look like it did nothing (unverified per-flag behaviour on 25.1).
OriginX / OriginY are in document units (Document.Unit) and are taken to be the centre of the view, not a corner (unverified).
Document.CreateView takes Zoom as a whole-number percent (long) while View.Zoom is a double; what CreateView's default Zoom of 0 does is unverified.
Views are saved inside the .cdr with the document, not in the workspace, so they travel with the file.
Activate acts on the active document window; with no window open there is nothing to apply it to (unverified error).
cards.example:
Dim v As Object
Set v = ActiveDocument.CreateView("Logo close-up", 4.25, 5.5, 400, ActiveDocument.ActivePage)
v.UseZoom = True
v.UsePage = True
' later, from any page:
ActiveDocument.Views.Item("Logo close-up").Activate
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: ViewHost
cards.summary: A UI-framework tab group (ICUIViewHost, from CrlFrmWkOM): one area of a frame window that holds document views as tabs. A script reads its ID and screen rectangle, lists the tabs it holds, and moves a view or another whole tab group into it. Confidence is low: this is framework plumbing with no visible design result.
use_for: move a document tab into another tab group, or merge two tab groups into one, from an add-in
read where a tab group sits on screen before a canvas screenshot
find which tab group a document window belongs to
avoid: plain tile or cascade: Windows.Arrange, or the frame window's TileViews / CombineViews
zoom or scroll: Window.ActiveView
cards.how: Members live on ICUIViewHost. It belongs to the UI framework, not the drawing model: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts (First, Find(ID) or Item), or from a document window: ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost. Views returns its tabs (ViewWindows); InsertView moves one ViewWindow into this host at a tab index; InsertViewHost moves all tabs of another host in.

key_members.name: ID
key_members.use: framework ID of the tab group

key_members.name: DockHost
key_members.use: the dock host this tab group sits in

key_members.name: DockItem
key_members.use: the group seen as a dock item

key_members.name: InsertView
key_members.use: move a ViewWindow into this group at a tab index

key_members.name: InsertViewHost
key_members.use: move every tab of another ViewHost into this group

gotchas: Framework objects (also_in CrlFrmWkOM) are not reachable from Document or Shape; go through Application.FrameWork or ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.
ID strings are generated by the framework at run time; do not hard-code them across sessions (unverified).
Position is in screen pixels, not document units, and changes when the user moves or resizes the UI.
Whether InsertView's Index counts tabs from 0 or 1 is not stated in the type library (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim vh As Object, vw As Object
Set vh = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost
Debug.Print vh.ID, vh.Views.Count
For Each vw In vh.Views
  Debug.Print vw.Title, vw.Kind
Next vw
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: use_for: InsertView/InsertViewHost only move tabs into an existing group; splitting tabs side by side is FrameWindow.TileViews or FrameWork.CreateFrameWindowForView, not this class

cards.name: ViewHosts
cards.summary: UI-framework collection of the tab groups (ViewHost objects) in one frame window (ICUIViewHosts, CrlFrmWkOM). A script counts them, walks them, finds one by ID, or takes the first or last. Confidence is low: framework plumbing with no visible design result.
use_for: detect whether documents are split into several tab groups before capturing the canvas
merge every tab group back into one from an add-in
avoid: listing documents or document windows: Application.Documents / Application.Windows
saved framings: Document.Views
cards.how: Members live on ICUIViewHosts. Reach it as Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts (the frame window's ViewHosts property); floating frame windows have their own, reached through FrameWork.FrameWindows. Item(Index), Find(ID), First, Last, Count, and For Each (_NewEnum).

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the tab groups

key_members.name: Find
key_members.use: a tab group by its ID

gotchas: Whether Item counts from 0 or 1 is not stated in the type library (unverified); First, Last and For Each avoid the question.
Only the tab groups of that one frame window are listed; a floating document frame is a separate frame window (FrameWork.FrameWindows).
Framework objects (also_in CrlFrmWkOM) are not reachable from Document or Shape; go through Application.FrameWork or ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.
cards.example:
Dim hosts As Object, h As Object
Set hosts = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts
Debug.Print hosts.Count
For Each h In hosts
  Debug.Print h.ID, h.Views.Count
Next h
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: Views
cards.summary: The collection of saved named views of one document (IVGViews), the list the View Manager docker shows. A script counts it, looks views up by 1-based index or name, and saves the current framing as a new view.
use_for: loop through every saved view of a layout to proof each framing in turn
save the current framing under a name from a review macro
check whether a template already ships with named views before adding more
avoid: controlling live zoom or scroll: use Window.ActiveView
listing open document windows: that is the Windows collection
cards.how: Members live on IVGViews. Reached as ActiveDocument.Views (Document.Views). Item takes a 1-based index or a view name; AddActiveView(Name) stores the active window's current page, zoom and origin as a new View and returns it; Count and For Each (_NewEnum) walk the list. Document.CreateView adds a view with explicit coordinates instead.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: a saved view by 1-based index or by name

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of saved views in the document

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the views

key_members.name: AddActiveView
key_members.use: save the active window's current framing under a name; returns the View

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Document that owns the views

gotchas: Item is base 1 (the type library says so); Item(0) fails.
Item with a name that does not exist raises a run-time error rather than returning Nothing (unverified); loop and compare Name when unsure.
AddActiveView captures the application's active window: activate the target document's window first when several documents are open (unverified for multi-document setups).
The collection has no Remove: delete a view with View.Delete.
cards.example:
Dim i As Long
For i = 1 To ActiveDocument.Views.Count
  Debug.Print i, ActiveDocument.Views.Item(i).Name
Next i
ActiveDocument.Views.AddActiveView "Proof framing"
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: ViewWindow
cards.summary: A UI-framework view tab (ICUIViewWindow, CrlFrmWkOM): one tab inside a tab group that hosts an application view, normally a document window. A script reads its ID, title, tooltip, kind, tab index and screen rectangle, activates or closes the tab, and gets the application-side object behind it (AppView). Confidence is low: framework plumbing.
use_for: get the on-screen rectangle of a document tab for a screenshot or a targeted click
bring a document tab to the front from an add-in
go from a UI tab to the drawing window or document it shows
avoid: document work (shapes, pages): use the Window and Document objects
closing a document: Document.Close
cards.how: Members live on ICUIViewWindow. From a document window: ActiveWindow.ViewWindow; from the framework: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts.First.Views (ViewWindows). ViewHost is the tab group it sits in, Index its tab position, Kind the type of view, AppView the application-side view object.

key_members.name: Kind
key_members.use: type of application view held in the tab

key_members.name: ViewHost
key_members.use: the tab group holding this view

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: bring the tab to the front

gotchas: AppView returns IDispatch; which object a drawing tab hands back (the VGCore Window or another view object) is not stated in the type library (unverified).
Kind is a string defined by the application, not an enum; read it at run time before branching on it (unverified values).
Position is in screen pixels and changes whenever the UI is moved or resized.
Close on the last view of a modified document may raise a save prompt that blocks an unattended run (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim vw As Object
Set vw = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow
Debug.Print vw.Title, vw.Kind, vw.Index
Debug.Print vw.ViewHost.ID
vw.Activate
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: ViewWindows
cards.summary: UI-framework collection of the view tabs (ViewWindow objects) in one tab group (ICUIViewWindows, CrlFrmWkOM), returned by ViewHost.Views. A script counts, walks, finds a tab by ID, or takes the first or last tab. Confidence is low: framework plumbing.
use_for: list every document tab in a tab group with its title
find a tab by ID and activate it
avoid: walking document windows in the drawing model: Application.Windows
saved framings: Document.Views
cards.how: Members live on ICUIViewWindows. Reach it as a ViewHost's Views property, e.g. ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost.Views or Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts.First.Views. Item(Index), Find(ID), First, Last, Count, and For Each (_NewEnum).

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of tabs in the group

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the tabs

gotchas: Whether Item counts from 0 or 1 is not stated in the type library (unverified); First, Last and For Each avoid the question.
It holds the tabs of one tab group only; walk ViewHosts to cover a split layout.
IDs are generated by the framework; do not hard-code them across sessions (unverified).
Framework objects (also_in CrlFrmWkOM) are not reachable from Document or Shape; go through Application.FrameWork or ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.
cards.example:
Dim tabs As Object, vw As Object
Set tabs = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost.Views
Debug.Print tabs.Count, tabs.First.Title, tabs.Last.Title
For Each vw In tabs
  Debug.Print vw.ID, vw.Title
Next vw
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

cards.name: Window
cards.summary: One document window (IVGWindow): the on-screen window or tab showing a document. Through it a script activates, closes, sizes or full-screens the window, reaches its ActiveView (zoom and scroll), redraws it, and converts between screen pixels and document coordinates.
use_for: switch between open layouts in a batch macro before working on each one
redraw the canvas after a long macro run with Application.Optimization on
open a second window on the same document to watch a detail while editing the whole page
map a screen position to page coordinates for a custom click tool
avoid: zooming or scrolling: that is ActiveView (Window.ActiveView.ToFitPage, Zoom, SetViewArea)
closing a document: use Document.Close, which handles the document rather than one of its windows
cards.how: Members live on IVGWindow. Reach it as ActiveWindow (Application.ActiveWindow), ActiveDocument.ActiveWindow, or Application.Windows.Item(n) / Document.Windows.Item(n). Document and Page say what it shows; ActiveView is its zoom and scroll; ViewWindow links to the UI-framework tab (ViewWindow / ViewHost).

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: bring this window (and its document) to the front

key_members.name: Document
key_members.use: the document shown in the window

key_members.name: Active
key_members.use: True when this is the active window

key_members.name: NewWindow
key_members.use: open another window on the same document

key_members.name: FullScreen
key_members.use: get or set the window's full-screen state (whether this is View > Full-screen Preview is unverified)

key_members.name: ScreenToDocument
key_members.use: screen pixel point to document coordinates (ByRef out)

key_members.name: DocumentToScreen
key_members.use: document point to screen pixels (ByRef out)

key_members.name: ViewWindow
key_members.use: the UI-framework tab hosting this window

gotchas: ActiveWindow is Nothing when no document is open; test it before use.
With tabbed documents, Left / Top / Width / Height and WindowState may be ignored or act on the tab group rather than a floating window (unverified).
ScreenToDocument / DocumentToScreen return their results through ByRef arguments; from Python win32com the outputs come back only with early binding (makepy) (unverified).
After a macro that sets Application.Optimization = True, set it back to False and call ActiveWindow.Refresh, or the canvas can stay stale.
Close on the last window of a modified document can raise a save prompt that blocks an unattended run (unverified).
Handle is the window handle of the document window (a long): a target for PostMessage instead of global keyboard input (unverified that the canvas acts on posted input).
cards.example:
Dim w As Object
Set w = ActiveDocument.ActiveWindow
Debug.Print w.Caption, w.Index, w.WindowState
w.ActiveView.ToFitPage
Application.Optimization = False
w.Refresh
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: FullScreen use no longer asserts it is the Full-screen Preview (unverified); Handle/PostMessage gotcha marked unverified

cards.name: Windows
cards.summary: A collection of document windows (IVGWindows): every window in the application (Application.Windows) or only one document's windows (Document.Windows). A script counts them, picks one by 1-based index, finds one by caption, tiles or cascades them, redraws them, or closes them all.
use_for: step through every open document window in a batch macro
tile two layouts side by side for a visual comparison
find a window by its caption (file name) and bring that layout forward
avoid: looping over documents to process them: use Application.Documents, because one document can have several windows
saved framings: those are Document.Views
cards.how: Members live on IVGWindows. Application.Windows holds every document window; ActiveDocument.Windows only that document's. Item(Index) is base 1; FindWindow(Caption) matches the window title; Arrange takes a cdrWindowArrangeStyle (cdrTileHorizontally 0, cdrTileVertically 1, cdrCascade 2); CloseAll closes every window in the collection.

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the windows

key_members.name: FindWindow
key_members.use: a document window by its caption

key_members.name: CloseAll
key_members.use: close every window in the collection

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the Application or Document that owns the collection

gotchas: Item is base 1.

Application.Windows.CloseAll closes every document window in the application, including documents the designer or another script opened; to stay inside your own work use YourDocument.Windows or Document.Close.
CloseAll on modified documents can raise save prompts that block an unattended run (unverified).
FindWindow needs the caption exactly as shown (a second window on the same file gets a suffix such as ':2', unverified); behaviour when nothing matches (Nothing or an error) is unverified.
Arrange (tile / cascade) is meant for floating document windows; with tabbed documents it may change the layout or do nothing (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim w As Object
For Each w In Application.Windows
  Debug.Print w.Index, w.Caption
Next w
Application.Windows.Arrange cdrTileVertically
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: CloseAll gotcha reworded: it closes all document windows in this CorelDRAW instance (no 'another process'), points to Document.Windows

cards.name: Workspace
cards.summary: One CorelDRAW workspace (IVGWorkspace): a saved UI layout of toolbars, dockers, menus and shortcuts, such as the default or a lite or Illustrator-style layout. A script reads its name and description, checks whether it is the default or the active one, and switches to it.
use_for: put an automation machine into a known workspace before a scripted UI run, so menus and dockers are where the script expects
report which workspace a designer is in when a macro misbehaves
toggle between a lite and a full layout from a macro button
avoid: creating, deleting or exporting a workspace: not in this class; use the Window/Workspace menu (New, Delete, Import, Export); Application.ImportWorkspace only imports workspace elements into the current workspace
anything about document content: a workspace is UI only
cards.how: Members live on IVGWorkspace. Reach it as Application.ActiveWorkspace or Application.Workspaces.Item(index or name). Name and Description are read-only, Default tells whether it is the default workspace, Active whether it is the current one, and Activate switches the UI to it.

key_members.name: Active
key_members.use: True when this workspace is in use

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: switch the UI to this workspace

gotchas: Activate rebuilds the toolbars, dockers and menus; it is slow and should not run in a loop or in the middle of an edit (unverified timing on 25.1).
Name is the display name, which may differ from the .cdws file name in the Workspace folder (unverified).
Everything except Activate is read-only: a workspace cannot be renamed or edited through this object.
The switch is likely to persist into the user's next session (unverified); store ActiveWorkspace first and restore it at the end of an automation run on a designer's machine.
cards.example:
Dim orig As Object, ws As Object
Set orig = Application.ActiveWorkspace
For Each ws In Application.Workspaces
  If ws.Default Then ws.Activate
Next ws
' ... scripted UI work ...
orig.Activate
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: avoid: Application.ImportWorkspace imports elements into the current workspace (typelib), it does not create one; example no longer hard-codes Item("Lite") (unverified display name) and switches to the Default workspace instead

cards.name: Workspaces
cards.summary: The collection of every workspace CorelDRAW has installed (IVGWorkspaces), the list behind Window > Workspace. A script counts the workspaces, walks them, and picks one by 1-based index or by name.
use_for: list the available workspaces to choose one for a scripted run
check that a team workspace is installed before a macro switches to it
avoid: adding a workspace: there is no Add; import a .cdws with the Window/Workspace/Import menu (Application.ImportWorkspace only imports workspace elements into the current workspace)
just the current workspace: Application.ActiveWorkspace is shorter
cards.how: Members live on IVGWorkspaces. Reach it as Application.Workspaces. Item(IndexOrName) takes a 1-based index or a workspace name; Count and For Each (_NewEnum) walk it; each element is a Workspace.

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: a workspace by 1-based index or by name

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: lets For Each walk the workspaces

gotchas: Item is base 1; a name that does not exist raises an error rather than returning Nothing (unverified).
The collection is read-only: no Add or Remove.
A workspace imported during the session may not show up in the list until CorelDRAW restarts (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim ws As Object
For Each ws In Application.Workspaces
  Debug.Print ws.Name, ws.Active, ws.Default
Next ws
cards.source: cdr_api_25 agent (VGCoreAuto.tlb harvest; coclass members read from the members_on interface)

review.changes: avoid: Application.ImportWorkspace does not add a workspace to the list, it imports elements into the current one (typelib)
